source_evidence.observation: For a general random variable X, properties (i)-(iv) are declared equivalent, with their positive parameters K_i differing by at most an absolute constant factor.

The four referenced properties are: a two-sided sub-gaussian tail bound; square-root growth of all L^p norms; a local quadratic-exponential MGF bound for X^2; and existence of a positive K_4 for which E exp(X^2/K_4^2) is at most 2.
Mean zero is imposed only for equivalence with the additional linear-MGF property (v); it is not an assumption of properties (i)-(iv).
The parameter comparison means that one absolute C works so that property i with K_i implies property j with K_j at most C K_i for any properties in the stated family.
A random variable satisfying one of the equivalent properties (i)-(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2 is called sub-gaussian.
The sub-gaussian norm is denoted ||X||_{psi_2} and is defined as inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}, described in the prose as the smallest K_4 in property (iv).

binders: X is a real-valued random variable [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2: X is called a random variable and is used with |X|, real powers, and real MGF parameters].
K_1, K_2, K_3, K_4 and the infimum variable t are positive real parameters where they occur [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(i)-(iv); PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, equation (2.13)].
conclusions: Definition of membership: X is sub-gaussian exactly when it satisfies one (and hence, by Proposition 2.5.2, all) of properties (i)-(iv) listed below, with existence of an appropriate positive parameter for each property [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, Definition 2.5.6; PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2].
Definition of the gauge: ||X||_{psi_2} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2} [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, Definition 2.5.6, equation (2.13)].
definitions_and_conventions: Property (i): there exists K_1 > 0 such that P{|X| >= t} <= 2 exp(-t^2/K_1^2) for every t >= 0 [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(i)].
Property (ii): there exists K_2 > 0 such that ||X||_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^(1/p) <= K_2 sqrt(p) for every p >= 1 [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(ii)].
Property (iii): there exists K_3 > 0 such that E exp(lambda^2 X^2) <= exp(K_3^2 lambda^2) for every real lambda satisfying |lambda| <= 1/K_3 [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(iii)].
Property (iv): there exists K_4 > 0 such that E exp(X^2/K_4^2) <= 2 [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(iv)].

The parameters witnessing the equivalent properties need not be identical; they are comparable only up to an absolute constant factor [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening and footnote 4].

The notation ||X||_{psi_2} names the infimum of all positive property-(iv) witnesses, not one of the tail or moment constants K_1, K_2, or K_3 [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, Definition 2.5.6 and equation (2.13)].
implicit_context: Probability and expectation are taken with respect to the underlying probability law of X [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(i)-(iv), structural use of P and E].

No assumption E X = 0 is required for sub-gaussian membership or for ||X||_{psi_2}; the source introduces mean zero only for the separate equivalence with property (v) [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, paragraph beginning 'Moreover'].

Because Definition 2.5.6 applies the norm definition to a sub-gaussian X, the admissible set in equation (2.13) is nonempty by property (iv) [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, Definition 2.5.6; PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(iv)].

details: Sub-gaussianity is existential in a positive witness K_i, while the tail and moment bounds quantify universally over t >= 0 or p >= 1 and property (iii) quantifies over all real lambda in its stated neighborhood [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2(i)-(iv)].
Satisfying any one of (i)-(iv) suffices; Definition 2.5.6 relies on Proposition 2.5.2 for their equivalence [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, Definition 2.5.6].
The gauge uses the exact threshold 2 and the exact expression exp(X^2/t^2), with t strictly positive [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, equation (2.13)].
The square applies to X and to the scale t; the expectation is outside the exponential [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, equation (2.13)].

The class includes non-centered random variables; mean zero is not part of Definition 2.5.6 [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening and the separate 'Moreover, if E X = 0' clause; PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, Definition 2.5.6].
Equation (2.13) defines a greatest-lower-bound value over all positive admissible scales; it does not add a witness-attainment requirement [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, equation (2.13)].

undebatable_constraints: The sub-gaussian predicate must be based on properties (i)-(iv) of Proposition 2.5.2, not on the mean-zero-only property (v) [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, Definition 2.5.6; PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2].
No centering hypothesis may be added to Definition 2.5.6 [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, the separate 'Moreover, if E X = 0' clause].
The psi_2 gauge must be the infimum over strictly positive real t satisfying E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2 [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, equation (2.13)].
The comparison in the gauge condition is <= 2, not equality and not a strict inequality [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, equation (2.13)].
The definition uses exp(X^2/t^2), not exp(|X|/t), exp(X/t), or a centered version of X [PDF p. 16, printed p. 27, equation (2.13)].

The constants witnessing properties (i)-(iv) are only equivalent up to absolute constant factors and must not be identified as the same numerical constant [PDF p. 13, printed p. 24, Proposition 2.5.2 opening and footnote 4].

ambiguities.issue: The prose says 'the smallest K_4', whereas equation (2.13) defines an infimum.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 16, printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 places the phrase 'smallest K_4' immediately before the infimum formula (2.13). For X identically zero, every positive t is admissible and the infimum is 0, so there is no smallest positive admissible K_4.
ambiguities.impact: The displayed formula should govern: formalize the gauge as an infimum and do not require the infimum to be attained by a positive witness.

ambiguities.issue: The cited passage does not explicitly spell out the codomain or the convention for possibly infinite expectations.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 13, printed page 24, Proposition 2.5.2 calls X merely a 'random variable', while its formulas use |X|, real p >= 1, real lambda, and exponential moments; PDF page 16, printed page 27, Definition 2.5.6 inherits that wording.
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must choose concrete real-valued-random-variable and expectation codomain conventions; those representational choices are not themselves specified by Definition 2.5.6.

contract_plain_english: A real-valued random variable is sub-gaussian when it has any one of the four equivalent behaviors in Proposition 2.5.2: Gaussian-type two-sided tails, L^p norms growing at most like sqrt(p), a suitable local exponential-moment bound for X^2, or one finite quadratic exponential moment bounded by 2. No mean-zero assumption is part of this definition. Its psi_2 norm is the infimum of all positive scales t for which E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2. The witnesses for the four characterizations are comparable up to universal constants, but they are not required to be numerically equal.
